steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with the gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths of visible light — particularly blue — are scattered much more strongly in all directions than longer wavelengths like red and orange. When you look at any part of the sky away from the sun, your eyes receive this scattered blue light, making the entire sky appear blue.
